title: The Corner: from Asylum Street to Cedar Hill, and the Bank That Was One Man
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Hartford, Asylum Street: the birth
stops.date_confidence: attested; Wikipedia and Strouse agree on the day and on the maternal grandfather's house
stops.campa: A son is born to Junius Spencer Morgan and Juliet Pierpont in her father's house on Asylum Street. They give him his mother's family name for a middle name, and he will use it in place of the first for the rest of his life: J. Pierpont Morgan, on every letter, every draft, every partnership deed. Hartford is a city that lends and insures rather than manufactures. Junius is already a merchant of standing and will shortly be a merchant of London, which is where the family money is about to be made. The child is born on the creditor's side of the ledger.
suggested_refs: 26 Asylum Street, Hartford, the Pierpont grandfather's house

stops.name: Boston, the English High School: the merchant's curriculum
stops.date_confidence: year attested, month and day unknown and defaulted to January. The coordinate is the Bedford Street building the school occupied 1844-1881, not the Warren Street building it moved to in 1881; the research pool's original coordinate for this stop pointed at Park Square and has been corrected
stops.campa: Junius moves the household to Boston and the boy enters the English High School, where the curriculum is arithmetic, bookkeeping, and commercial correspondence rather than Greek. The building on Bedford Street is shared with the Latin School: one set of boys construing Homer, another set balancing accounts, the same roof over both. He is fourteen, and he is put with the boys balancing accounts. Nothing in the course is meant to be pursued for its own sake. It is the last full stretch of ordinary schooling he has in his own country.
suggested_refs: The Bedford Street schoolhouse shared by English High and Boston Latin, 1844-1881

stops.name: Ponta Delgada, the Azores: sent away to mend
stops.date_confidence: attested to April 1852; day unknown and defaulted to 01. The length of the stay is given in the sources only as months
stops.campa: A severe attack of rheumatic fever leaves him unable to walk, and his father sends him alone across the Atlantic to the Azores to recover. He spends months at Ponta Delgada among strangers, on an island of volcanic soil and orange groves, fifteen years old and out of reach of every doctor his family trusts. He comes back able to walk, and for the rest of his life a failing body is answered by putting him on a ship. What he did through those months is not recorded. The sources give the length of the stay as months and give nothing else at all.
sources: J. P. Morgan dossier, chronological reconstruction
suggested_refs: Ponta Delgada, Sao Miguel, the convalescent island of 1852

stops.name: La Tour-de-Peilz, the Bellerive school
stops.date_confidence: year attested, month and day unknown and defaulted to January
stops.campa: He is sent to the Bellerive school at La Tour-de-Peilz on Lake Geneva, above the vineyards between Vevey and Montreux, to sharpen his French. Junius is building an Anglo-American banking house and wants a son who can be received in London and on the continent without an interpreter standing behind him. The schooling is deliberate, and it is not a university education pursued for its own sake; it is the manufacture of a partner. He is nineteen and has now been schooled in three countries. The next year his father sends him on to Germany.
suggested_refs: The Bellerive boarding school at La Tour-de-Peilz, near Vevey

stops.name: Gottingen, the Georgia Augusta: the degree that may not exist
stops.date_confidence: attendance across 1856-1857 attested; month and day unknown and defaulted to January. The art-history degree is [R]: English Wikipedia states he earned one in six months, the university's own record supports roughly a year in residence with lectures in mathematics and chemistry and daily German, and Jean Strouse's biography does not support the degree. The two lenses of the research pool contradicted each other on this point and it is left unresolved here
stops.campa: At the Georgia Augusta he takes lectures in mathematics and chemistry and hires a tutor for daily German. Tradition, repeated down to the present, holds that he earned a degree in art history here in six months, and it is the one credential ever produced to explain the collector he became. The university record supports about a year in residence and no such degree, and Strouse does not support it either. He leaves in the summer of 1857 with fluent German and an appetite for buying. Nobody since has been able to put a hand on the diploma.
sources: University of Gottingen institutional history, as characterized in the J. P. Morgan dossier
suggested_refs: The matriculation registers of the University of Gottingen for 1856-1857

segments.name: The Clerk on Both Sides of the Wire

stops.name: London, George Peabody and Company: the family firm
stops.date_confidence: attested to August 1857; day unknown and defaulted to 01
stops.campa: He crosses to London and takes a desk at George Peabody and Company on Old Broad Street, where his father is partner and heir apparent. The business is Anglo-American: British capital placed into American railroads, American cotton and grain sold into Britain, two economies stitched together by a house whose credit is its only real asset. He is twenty, and he is learning the mechanism from inside a firm that will be his in thirty-three years. What he is learning is not a trade in goods but the pricing of other people's promises. The following year the house sends him to New York.
suggested_refs: 22 Old Broad Street, City of London, the Peabody counting house

stops.name: New York, Duncan, Sherman and Company: the junior man
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1858; month and day unknown and defaulted to January. The chronology lens and the geography lens agree on the firm and on the years 1858-1861
stops.campa: He arrives in New York as a junior clerk at Duncan, Sherman and Company, the American correspondent of the Peabody house, and is put on foreign exchange and trade finance. The city he enters is a port with a stock exchange attached; the country behind it is laying track faster than anybody can account for. He is a merchant's son on a salary, learning the difference between what a bill of exchange says and what it is worth on the day it is presented. His father reads the letters home as reports from a subordinate branch.
sources: J. P. Morgan dossier, chronological reconstruction
suggested_refs: Duncan, Sherman and Company, Wall Street, correspondent of George Peabody and Co.

stops.name: New Orleans, the cotton correspondents
stops.date_confidence: attested to early 1859; month and day unknown and defaulted to January. The purchase of a cargo on his own initiative is told in several biographies and is not carried by the research pool, so it is left out here
stops.campa: The house sends its junior man south to the cotton correspondents. He goes down the river to New Orleans, where the crop that pays for the whole Anglo-American trade is graded, warehoused, and sold, and where the men handling it are selling to Liverpool through firms like his own. It is his apprenticeship in a commodity rather than in a ledger, in the one American crop whose price is set on another continent. The men grading the bales are two years from being enemy nationals. He is twenty-one years old.
suggested_refs: The New Orleans cotton exchange district, 1859

stops.name: 53 Exchange Place, his own name over the door
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown and defaulted to January
stops.campa: He opens his own house at 53 Exchange Place under his own name: J. Pierpont Morgan and Company, one room, one clerk, and the credit of his father's London firm standing invisibly behind everything he signs. He is twenty-four. The country is coming apart that spring, which is to say that gold, cotton, arms, and government paper are all about to move violently, and a young man with London credit and a New York address stands where the movement will pass. Fort Sumter is fired on in April.
suggested_refs: 53 Exchange Place, first premises of J. Pierpont Morgan and Company

segments.name: Memie, and the Business of the War

stops.name: New York, the Hall carbines
stops.date_confidence: the loan is attested to 1861; month and day unknown, set to June to order the segment before the October wedding. The 1863 congressional committee denounced arms profiteering in general and did not charge Morgan; the moral reading of the episode differs between Wasson, who defends him, and Myers and Josephson, who do not, and the research pool carries this only through the dossier's summary
stops.campa: He lends twenty thousand dollars to Simon Stevens against surplus Hall carbines, condemned government arms bought cheap and resold to General Fremont's command at many times their cost. The loan is repaid. A congressional committee denounces the traffic in arms two years later without charging him, and biographers have argued the case both ways ever since, routine secured lending on one side and profiteering on the other, working from an identical set of documents. He is twenty-four. Which of them is right cannot be settled from the papers that survive.
sources: J. P. Morgan dossier, chronological reconstruction citing the 1863 congressional investigation and biographers R. Gordon Wasson, Gustavus Myers, Matthew Josephson and Charles R. Morris
suggested_refs: The 1863 congressional investigation into arms contracting
R. Gordon Wasson, The Hall Carbine Affair (1948)

stops.name: 5 East Fourteenth Street, the marriage to Memie
stops.date_confidence: attested to October 1861; day unknown and defaulted to 01
stops.campa: Amelia Sturges, called Memie, is too ill with tuberculosis to stand at her own wedding. He marries her at her family's house on East Fourteenth Street in front of a handful of people and carries her down to the carriage himself. He has closed the office to do it and does not reopen it. Both families understand the marriage as a race, and he has decided to run it: within days he takes her out of the New York winter, bound for the Mediterranean and whatever air might hold her.
suggested_refs: The Sturges family house at 5 East Fourteenth Street

stops.name: Algiers, the search for a climate
stops.date_confidence: the Algiers leg is carried by the dossier and corroborated in outline by Wikipedia's account of the journey to Nice; the month is inferred from the October departure and the February death and is set to December to order the segment
stops.campa: He carries his wife through Algiers looking for a climate. The medicine of the age holds that consumption yields to warm dry air, so the honeymoon becomes an itinerary of treatment: steamers, hotels, physicians consulted in three languages, a banker of twenty-four with an invalid on his arm working down the North African coast and back. She does not improve. He writes to Junius in the voice of a man rendering an account of a position that is moving against him. Nobody has offered any remedy but movement, so he keeps moving her. In the new year they cross to Nice.
sources: J. P. Morgan dossier, corroborated by Wikipedia's account of the journey to Nice
suggested_refs: The winter invalid route of the 1860s: Algiers, Nice, and the Riviera cure

stops.name: Nice, the death of Amelia Sturges Morgan
stops.date_confidence: attested to February 1862, four months after the wedding; day unknown and defaulted to 01
stops.campa: Four months after the wedding Amelia Sturges Morgan dies at Nice. He is twenty-four and a widower. He brings her body home for burial and returns to the single room at Exchange Place, and the office reopens as though the winter had been a business trip. He will marry again within three years and father four children. His biographers reach for these four months to explain the silences of the next fifty years. Of Algiers and of Nice he himself leaves nothing in any document that survives.
suggested_refs: Jean Strouse, Morgan: American Financier, on the Sturges marriage

stops.name: New York, the gold shipped to London
stops.date_confidence: the episode is carried by the dossier's chronological reconstruction only; the underlying primary sources were not re-fetched in this pass and the month and day are unknown and defaulted to January
stops.campa: With an associate he buys gold in New York and ships it out through his father's London house while the currency of a country at war swings on every rumor from the front. Buying gold with greenbacks is legal. It is also, to a Union at war, a wager that the Union will do badly, and the newspapers treat it accordingly. He makes money on it and nobody prosecutes. His enemies keep the episode in hand for the next fifty years. It reaches us through a single chronological summary whose own citations have not been checked against a document.
sources: J. P. Morgan dossier, chronological reconstruction
suggested_refs: The wartime gold market of 1864 and the greenback exchange rate

stops.name: Wall Street, Dabney, Morgan and Company
stops.date_confidence: the partnership is dated 1864-1871 by the dossier; the month is unknown and set to September to order it after the gold episode of the same year
stops.campa: Charles Dabney, an older man with a reputation for exactness, puts his name in front of Morgan's, and for seven years the house is Dabney, Morgan and Company: American securities sold into Europe, European capital placed into American railroads, his father's London firm at the far end of every transaction. The war ends in the middle of it and the country begins laying track at a rate that will need more capital than the country has. In the market's eyes he is still Junius Morgan's son in New York.
sources: J. P. Morgan dossier, chronological reconstruction
suggested_refs: Dabney, Morgan and Company, Wall Street, 1864-1871

stops.name: St. George's, Stuyvesant Square: the marriage to Fanny
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. The coordinate is Wikipedia's for St. George's at 209 East 16th Street; the geography lens of the research pool gave a point some 170 metres southeast and has been corrected here and at the 1913 funeral stop
stops.campa: He marries Frances Louisa Tracy, called Fanny, at St. George's on Stuyvesant Square, the parish where he has already begun the lay service that will occupy him for the rest of his life. He becomes senior warden, pays for the industrial school and the soup kitchen, and New York comes to call the place Morgan's Church. Four children follow: Louisa in 1866, John Pierpont junior in 1867, Juliet in 1870, Anne in 1873. The marriage lasts forty-eight years, much of it conducted on separate continents.
suggested_refs: St. George's Episcopal Church, 209 East 16th Street, Stuyvesant Square

segments.name: The Corner and the House on Madison Avenue

stops.name: 23 Wall Street, Drexel, Morgan and Company
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: Anthony Drexel of Philadelphia proposes a partnership, and on the first of July Drexel, Morgan and Company opens at the corner of Wall and Broad. Drexel brings Philadelphia standing and capital, Morgan brings the London house at the far end of every wire, and the address itself supplies the name: for forty years the men who mean this house will say only the Corner. He is thirty-four. The railroads are the business, and the railroads are at war with one another.
sources: J. P. Morgan dossier, chronological reconstruction
suggested_refs: 23 Wall Street, the Corner, from 1871

stops.name: 23 Wall Street, the paper of the Edison Electric Light Company
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1878; month and day unknown and defaulted to January. The coordinate is inherited byte-identical from thomas_edison.journey.json, which pins 23 Wall Street at 40.7069, -74.0113; the geography lens of this pool gives 40.7069, -74.01 for the same building, a discrepancy of about ninety metres that is noted rather than resolved
stops.campa: Thomas Edison has no working lamp when the Corner begins financing him. Drexel, Morgan and Company takes the paper of the Edison Electric Light Company on the strength of a promise about incandescence, and Morgan's own name is on the subscription list. It is the first time he backs an invention rather than a railroad or a government. The terms are the terms he applies to everything: money in exchange for control of the enterprise the money makes possible. Edison signs them.
suggested_refs: The 1878 subscription list of the Edison Electric Light Company

stops.name: 219 Madison Avenue, the house lit by Edison
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. 219 Madison is the residence; the library built beside it in 1906 is 225 Madison, and the two addresses are conflated in one item of the research pool
stops.campa: Edison's men run wire through the Madison Avenue house and set a steam generator in a shed behind it, and the residence becomes one of the first in America lit throughout by electric light. The installation smokes, sets a desk alight, and requires an engineer living on the premises to keep it going. The Corner is holding the paper of the company that built it, so the house is both a residence and an argument. Morgan keeps it. He brings the neighbourhood in after dark to look at the lamps burning in every room of the house at once.
suggested_refs: The generator shed behind 219 Madison Avenue, 1882

stops.name: The Corsair on the Hudson, the railroad presidents afloat
stops.date_confidence: the Corsair conferences are dated 1889-1890 by the dossier; the month is unknown and set to July to order the segment. The 1883 private placement of William H. Vanderbilt's New York Central stock mentioned in the campa is tagged [R] in the research pool
stops.campa: He takes the presidents of the western trunk lines aboard the Corsair and puts the yacht out into the Hudson, where nobody can leave the conversation. The rate wars have been ruining the roads and the bondholders his house sold them to; the men aboard have spent years cutting each other's throats for freight. Six years earlier he had quietly placed a great block of William H. Vanderbilt's New York Central stock rather than let it hit the market at once. No law obliges any of them to be aboard. They come back to the dock having agreed to rates that are, in the words of the agreement, public, reasonable, uniform and stable.
sources: J. P. Morgan dossier, chronological reconstruction
suggested_refs: The Corsair agreements of 1889-1890 and the Interstate Commerce Act of 1887

stops.name: Monte Carlo, the death of Junius Spencer Morgan
stops.date_confidence: the accident is attested to 3 April 1890 and the death to 8 April 1890, five days later, still unconscious; the research pool gave only April 1890 and the mechanism, and the day has been corrected from the Junius Spencer Morgan record
stops.campa: Junius Spencer Morgan's horses bolt at an oncoming train on the road above Monte Carlo. The carriage strikes a pile of stone and throws him against a wall. He breaks a wrist and takes a concussion, never regains consciousness, and dies five days later. Pierpont is fifty-three, and with the London house and the fortune he inherits the end of the only authority that had stood over him. The body is carried back across the Atlantic and buried in the family plot at Cedar Hill in Hartford.
sources: J. P. Morgan dossier, chronological reconstruction
suggested_refs: The Morgan family plot at Cedar Hill Cemetery, Hartford

stops.name: Prince's Gate, Kensington: two houses knocked together
stops.date_confidence: undated in the research pool, which gives only 'various'; set to June 1890 to follow the inheritance of the London house and to order the segment
stops.campa: He takes over his father's London house at Number 13 Prince's Gate, by Hyde Park, then buys Number 14 and knocks the two together, because the pictures no longer fit. London is where the collection lives. English portraits, Chinese porcelain, illuminated manuscripts, bought through dealers who understand that his standing offer is a whole collection rather than the best piece in it. For twenty years he keeps two households and two nationalities of business, and the American newspapers report the purchases as news from abroad.
suggested_refs: 13-14 Prince's Gate, Kensington, the London collection house

stops.name: 1 East 60th Street, the Metropolitan Club
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1891 by the dossier; month and day unknown and defaulted to January
stops.campa: His friend John King is blackballed at the Union Club. Morgan answers by founding a club of his own: he donates the Fifth Avenue site at Sixtieth Street, commissions Stanford White to design the house, and takes the presidency himself. An institution that will not accommodate him is answered by a second institution that will, which is a method he applies afterward to whole industries. The house goes up on the corner and opens in 1894. New York calls it the Millionaires' Club. He is its first president.
sources: J. P. Morgan dossier, chronological reconstruction
suggested_refs: The Metropolitan Club, 1 East 60th Street, Stanford White, 1894

stops.name: New York, the making of General Electric
stops.date_confidence: the merger is attested to 1892; month and day unknown and defaulted to January. The consolidation of Edison's separate companies into Edison General Electric is separately attested to 24 April 1889 and is folded into this stop
stops.campa: The Corner has already gathered Edison's scattered companies into the Edison General Electric Company. Now the bankers merge that with Thomson-Houston, the rival with better management and enough patents to fight a long war over, and the surviving company is called General Electric. Edison's name comes off the door. He is neither president nor director of the new company, and the lamp, the station and the wire stand exactly as he built them, under a name that is not his. He sells his stock.
suggested_refs: The 1892 Edison General Electric and Thomson-Houston merger agreement

stops.name: Washington, the gold for the Treasury
stops.date_confidence: attested to February 1895; day unknown and defaulted to 01. The bond figure of about $62 million is the dossier's summary of the public record and was not re-fetched from a primary Treasury source. The reported $250,000 to McKinley's 1896 campaign, mentioned at the end of the campa, rests on campaign-finance historians cited in the dossier and not on a primary ledger
stops.campa: The federal gold reserve is draining at a rate that will empty it in weeks and the Cleveland administration has no lawful way to stop it. Morgan goes to Washington, produces a Civil War statute that lets the Treasury buy coin without going to Congress, and with the Belmont and Rothschild houses contracts to deliver some sixty-two million dollars in gold against thirty-year bonds. The reserve holds. The syndicate profits, the country notices, and the free-silver campaign of the following year runs against him by name. He answers it with a reported quarter of a million dollars to McKinley.
sources: J. P. Morgan dossier, chronological reconstruction of the 1895 gold syndicate and the 1896 campaign contribution
suggested_refs: The February 1895 Treasury bond contract under the Act of 14 March 1900's predecessor statute of 1862

stops.name: West 44th Street, the ground for the yacht club
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1898; month and day unknown and defaulted to January. Morgan was commodore 1897-1899. The coordinate has been corrected to 37 West 44th Street; the research pool's point sat about 200 metres east, near Fifth Avenue. The quote on this stop is [R], attributed to him in a 1961 business-education periodical and not traceable to any document in his lifetime
stops.campa: As commodore of the New York Yacht Club he buys the plot on West Forty-fourth Street, seventy-five feet by a hundred, for a hundred and forty-eight thousand dollars, and hands the club the ground for its new house. The yacht in his life is not a recreation. It is an office that can be moved out of reach of the shore, and the rate agreements he imposed on the railroads were signed aboard one Corsair or another. The men he houses here are the men who sat at those tables. He is commodore for two years, and the clubhouse on the plot is finished in 1901.
stops.quote: If you have to ask the price, you can't afford it.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to Morgan on the cost of a yacht, per Business Education World (Gregg Publishing Company, 1961) as cited by Wikiquote; not located in any document of his lifetime
suggested_refs: The New York Yacht Club house at 37 West 44th Street, Warren and Wetmore, 1901

stops.name: Wardenclyffe, Shoreham: the contract with Tesla
stops.date_confidence: the contract is attested to March 1901; day unknown and defaulted to 01. The sum of $150,000 and the 51 percent interest in the company and in present and future wireless patents are attested. That Tesla privately intended broadcast power while pitching telegraphy is carried by nikola_tesla.journey.json
stops.campa: Nikola Tesla comes to him for the money to put wireless telegraphy across the Atlantic, and in March he signs: a hundred and fifty thousand dollars against fifty-one percent of the company and of the wireless patents, present and future. Stanford White designs the tower and the brick laboratory at Shoreham on Long Island. What Tesla has pitched is telegraphy. What Tesla intends, and does not say, is the transmission of power itself, broadcast through the earth to anyone standing on it. The contract is for the first thing.
suggested_refs: The March 1901 Morgan-Tesla agreement and the Wardenclyffe patents schedule

stops.name: 23 Wall Street, United States Steel
stops.date_confidence: the incorporation in New Jersey is attested to 2 March 1901; the research pool dated it February 1901, which is when the terms were settled, and the date has been corrected. The Schwab dinner of December 1900 and the ensuing Carnegie negotiations are attested. The quote is [R]: Ida Tarbell reports it in 1925, twelve years after Morgan's death, and the wording here restores the word 'me' that the research pool's transcription dropped
stops.campa: Charles Schwab describes an integrated steel combination over dinner in December, and Morgan spends the winter buying it. Andrew Carnegie sells outright for two hundred and twenty-five million in fifty-year gold bonds; Federal Steel and National Steel come in; Rockefeller's Mesabi ore ranges and lake fleet are bought that spring out of 26 Broadway for about ninety million. United States Steel is incorporated in New Jersey on the second of March, capitalised at one billion four hundred million dollars, the first billion-dollar corporation on earth. Frick takes a board seat and never runs a mill again. The chairman is Elbert Gary, a lawyer.
stops.quote: Well, I don't know as I want a lawyer to tell me what I cannot do. I hire him to tell me how to do what I want to do.
stops.quote_source: Ida M. Tarbell, The Life of Elbert H. Gary: The Story of Steel (1925), p. 109, reporting Morgan; secondhand, twelve years after his death
suggested_refs: The U.S. Steel certificate of incorporation, New Jersey, 2 March 1901

stops.name: Wall Street, the Northern Pacific corner
stops.date_confidence: the corner and the panic are attested to May 1901; the ninth is the day of the general market break and the research pool gives only the month. The quote is [R]: the words are widely attested in the secondary literature in connection with this episode, but the usual citation to the New York World of 11 May 1901 could not be verified, Chronicling America's API having been retired, and one book dates the remark to 1924, eleven years after Morgan's death
stops.campa: Morgan and James Hill are buying Northern Pacific shares to hold the road. Edward Harriman and Kuhn, Loeb are buying the same shares to take it. Between them they buy more stock than exists. The shorts cannot deliver, the price runs to a thousand dollars a share, and the rest of the market is sold off to cover the corner, ruining men who had nothing to do with either side. The two camps settle by putting the road into a holding company called Northern Securities. Nobody is prosecuted for the panic and nobody ruined by it is made whole.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to Morgan in connection with the 1901 Northern Pacific corner; printed as an epigraph in Richard O'Connor, Iron Wheels and Broken Men, and in Stewart H. Holbrook, James J. Hill; the standard citation to the New York World of 11 May 1901 is unverified
sources: J. P. Morgan dossier, chronological reconstruction of the May 1901 corner
suggested_refs: The Northern Securities Company organisation agreement, 1901

stops.name: New York and London, the International Mercantile Marine
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1902; month and day unknown and defaulted to January. The British legislative response is well documented but is not carried by the research pool and is stated here only in general terms
stops.campa: He assembles the shipping the way he assembled the steel. The American lines and the British lines are bought or bound into a single combination, the International Mercantile Marine Company, with the White Star Line inside it. British opinion treats the purchase as a national loss and the government moves to keep the fastest ships under a British flag. The combination never earns what he paid for it. It is the one great assembly of his life that does not work, and the record does not show him saying why.
suggested_refs: The International Mercantile Marine Company prospectus, 1902

stops.name: Wardenclyffe, the letter that ends it
stops.date_confidence: the refusal is attested to 14 July 1903; the research pool dated it variously to July 1901 and to 1904 and both have been corrected. That Morgan refused because wireless power could not be metered is [R] and unsupported: no located Morgan document states it, and the Wardenclyffe record gives only the cost overruns, the change of scope, and Marconi's December 1901 transatlantic signal
stops.campa: Marconi has already put a signal across the Atlantic with equipment costing a fraction of the tower at Shoreham, and Tesla's plans have grown from telegraphy into the broadcast of power, his costs growing with them. Morgan pays out the contracted hundred and fifty thousand, demands an accounting, and refuses everything after it. The legend that grows around this refusal says he asked where the meter would go; no document in his hand says anything of the kind. In July the office writes that it will be impossible for him to do anything in the matter. Tesla goes on writing. The tower stands unfinished on Long Island.
suggested_refs: Morgan's letter of 14 July 1903 to Nikola Tesla

stops.name: The Capitol, Northern Securities dissolved
stops.date_confidence: the decision and the 5-4 split are attested to 14 March 1904. The coordinate is the Capitol, where the Court sat in the old Senate chamber in 1904; the research pool's point was the Supreme Court building on First Street, which was not built until 1935
stops.campa: The government sues the holding company under the Sherman Act, and the Court divides five to four against it and orders the combination dissolved. Morgan is a named defendant in a civil judgment. Nothing criminal is charged and nobody goes anywhere. The decision does not touch United States Steel, which is larger and was assembled by outright purchase rather than by holding company. What the decision establishes is narrow and new, that the government may say no to him and be obeyed. He is sixty-six years old. The company is dissolved.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Northern Securities Co. v. United States'
suggested_refs: Northern Securities Co. v. United States, 193 U.S. 197 (1904)

stops.name: Fifth Avenue, the presidency of the Metropolitan Museum
stops.date_confidence: trustee from 1888, vice president, then president from 1904 until his death in 1913; the month and day of his accession to the presidency are unknown and defaulted to January. The quote is [R]: Smithsonian Magazine attributes it to him without naming a letter, an interview, or any document
stops.campa: Trustee, then vice president, and from this year president of the Metropolitan Museum of Art until he dies. He buys for the museum and he buys for himself, and the difference between the two is a matter of where the crates are sent. He funds excavation in Egypt, hires men who know more than he does and lets them spend, and moves through the European trade as the buyer of last resort, the one bidder whose entry ends an auction. Roger Fry works for him and finds him impossible. Joseph Duveen sells to him and grows rich.
stops.quote: No price is too great for a work of unquestioned beauty and known authenticity.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to Morgan in Smithsonian Magazine, 'J. P. Morgan, Cutthroat Capitalist'; the magazine cites no letter, interview, or document for the line
suggested_refs: The Metropolitan Museum trustees' minutes, 1904-1913, and the Egyptian Expedition

stops.name: 225 Madison Avenue, McKim's library
stops.date_confidence: completion attested to 1906; month and day unknown and defaulted to January. The address is 225 Madison at 36th Street; 219 Madison next door is the residence, and one item of the research pool conflates the two
stops.campa: Charles Follen McKim builds him a marble library beside the house on Madison Avenue. Into it go the manuscripts and the early printed books, bought by the collection rather than by the item, and Belle da Costa Greene, his librarian since 1905, runs the room and outbids the dealers of Europe on his behalf. It is not a public building and is not intended to become one. It is a private room, and Morgan had told the architect what he wanted of it: a gem.
suggested_refs: The McKim building, 225 Madison Avenue at East 36th Street, completed 1906

stops.name: The American Museum of Natural History, and a stone named after him
stops.date_confidence: the naming is attested to a meeting of the New York Academy of Sciences on 5 December 1910; the coordinate here is the American Museum of Natural History, which he endowed and which received the gems, not the Academy meeting room, whose venue the research pool does not fix
stops.campa: He gives to the American Museum of Natural History as he gives to hospitals, to churches, and to the Metropolitan: in cash, in gems, in whole collections bought entire and handed across. On the fifth of December the gemmologist George Frederick Kunz rises at the New York Academy of Sciences and proposes the name morganite for a pink beryl found that year in fine colour on an island off Madagascar, in honour of the gems Morgan has given to New York and to Paris. The stone is pink, transparent, and takes a facet well.
suggested_refs: The Morgan gem collections at the American Museum of Natural History and the Museum national d'Histoire naturelle, Paris

stops.name: 225 Madison Avenue, the library as a command post
stops.date_confidence: attested to 19 October 1907, the day of his return from the Episcopal convention at Richmond. The coordinate is within about fifty metres of Wikipedia's value for the library and is retained from the research pool
stops.campa: He is at an Episcopal convention in Richmond when the trust companies begin to go. He comes north overnight, and by the morning of the nineteenth the library on Thirty-sixth Street is a clearing house: teams of young accountants sent through the books of one institution after another in the dark, reporting back which are sound and which are not, while the presidents of the sound ones sit in the West Room waiting to be told what they will contribute. He is seventy years old and holds no public office. There is no central bank in the United States.
suggested_refs: Robert Bruner and Sean Carr, The Panic of 1907

stops.name: The Corner, the two verdicts
stops.date_confidence: both verdicts are attested to 22 October 1907. The stop is pinned at the Corner, where Morgan worked that day; the Knickerbocker's own doors were on Fifth Avenue and the Trust Company of America's on Wall Street, and neither address is pinned in the research pool
stops.campa: The verdict on the Knickerbocker Trust Company is that it cannot be saved, and it is not: the run takes some eight million dollars out of it in three hours and the doors close before noon. The verdict on the Trust Company of America is that it can be, and eight and a quarter million is put together to hold it open. What separates the two verdicts is an audit made overnight in a private library by men nobody elected. Outside the Trust Company of America the queue stretches round the block, and the cash goes up the steps in bags.
suggested_refs: The Knickerbocker Trust Company suspension, 22 October 1907

stops.name: 18 Broad Street, the exchange kept open
stops.date_confidence: the research pool dates this only to October 1907 and gives the outline rather than the sums; the 24th is the standard date for the call-money crisis on the floor and is used here to order the segment. The specific figures raised that afternoon differ between accounts and are left out
stops.campa: Call money on the floor has gone to rates no broker can pay, and the president of the Stock Exchange crosses Broad Street to tell Morgan he must close it. Morgan tells him the exchange will not close. Within the hour the presidents of the national banks are in the room and the money for the floor is subscribed, and word of it goes across the floor before the bell. He holds no office, no charter, and no authority to do any of this. The exchange does not close.
suggested_refs: The New York Stock Exchange call-money market, October 1907

stops.name: The East Room, the door locked until morning
stops.date_confidence: the conference is attested to the evening of Saturday 2 November 1907, with agreement reached about 4:45 a.m. on Sunday the 3rd and Roosevelt's antitrust clearance following on Monday the 4th before the markets opened. The research pool dated the conference itself to 4 November, conflating it with the clearance, and this has been corrected
stops.campa: On the Saturday evening he brings the trust company presidents and the bankers into the library, puts one group in the East Room and the other in the West, locks the front door and keeps the key in his pocket. The brokerage of Moore and Schley is holding Tennessee Coal and Iron as collateral and will fail without relief. The agreement comes at a quarter to five in the morning: United States Steel buys Tennessee Coal and Iron, Moore and Schley stands, and on Monday Roosevelt clears the antitrust question in Washington before the markets open.
suggested_refs: The U.S. Steel acquisition of the Tennessee Coal, Iron and Railroad Company, November 1907

stops.name: Aix-les-Bains, the berth not taken
stops.date_confidence: the sinking is attested to 15 April 1912 and Morgan's booked suite and changed plans are attested; that he was specifically at Aix-les-Bains taking the waters is [R], carried by the dossier and by popular accounts and not confirmed by any source re-fetched in this pass
stops.campa: A suite with a private promenade deck is held for him on the maiden voyage of the White Star liner his own combination owns. He does not sail. The Titanic goes down in the North Atlantic with the ship, the line, and the combination all belonging to him on paper, and the suite with its private promenade deck goes down empty. The accepted account puts him at Aix-les-Bains in Savoy, taking the waters, an old man's spring cure. He is seventy-five. No reachable source actually places him in the town, and where he stood on the morning of the fifteenth is not established.
suggested_refs: The White Star Line under the International Mercantile Marine Company, 1912

stops.name: Capitol Hill, the Pujo committee
stops.date_confidence: the testimony is dated 18-19 December 1912 by the dossier, and the New York Times reported his appearance on 19 December; a fetch of Wikipedia's Pujo Committee article could not independently confirm the exact dates. The famous exchange on character is [R]: the primary hearing transcript could not be retrieved, several government-hosted pages having refused the fetch. The quote used here is [A], seen in a fetched PDF that quotes the testimony verbatim and cites it
stops.campa: Samuel Untermyer has spent months mapping the interlocking directorates of what the committee calls the money trust, and now he has the man himself in the chair. Morgan is seventy-five, ill, and answers for two days. Asked whether commercial credit rests first upon money or upon property, he answers that it rests first upon character; asked whether a man of doubtful character could borrow against the best security in the world, he says no. His partners will say afterward that the two days killed him. He dies three months later.
stops.quote: Because a man I do not trust could not get money from me on all the bonds in Christendom.
stops.quote_source: J. P. Morgan, testimony before the Pujo Committee, December 1912, quoted verbatim in Jon R. Moen and Mary Tone Rodgers, 'How J. P. Morgan Picked the Winners and Losers in the Panic of 1907,' Essays in Economic & Business History 40 (2022), p. 172
sources: Moen and Rodgers, Essays in Economic & Business History 40 (2022)
suggested_refs: The Pujo Committee hearings, digitised and searchable at FRASER, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
The open letter of J. P. Morgan & Co. to the Pujo committee, 1913

stops.name: Rome, the Grand Hotel Plaza
stops.date_confidence: the death, the city, the date and the age are attested. The hotel is now independently corroborated: the Italian Wikipedia article names the Albergo Roma, the future Grand Hotel Plaza. The coordinate is the hotel at Via del Corso 126; the research pool's afterlife lens used the Rome centroid about 1.4 km away and its geography lens a point near Piazza Barberini, and both have been corrected
stops.campa: He has been failing since the winter, with nervous exhaustion and difficulty swallowing and physicians in attendance. He dies in his sleep at the hotel on the Via del Corso, the Albergo Roma that will become the Grand Hotel Plaza, seventy-five years old, in a rented room in a city he had come to as a collector. There is no poisoning, no mystery, and nothing to investigate, which has never stopped anyone from saying otherwise. The body is brought home to New York aboard the French liner France.
suggested_refs: The Grand Hotel Plaza, Via del Corso 126, Rome

stops.name: St. George's, the funeral
stops.date_confidence: the funeral is attested to April 1913 after the body's return aboard the France; the day is not given in the research pool and is defaulted to 01. Coordinate corrected to Wikipedia's value for the church, as at the 1865 marriage stop
stops.campa: He is carried into St. George's on Stuyvesant Square, the parish he served as senior warden for thirty years and paid for outright: the industrial school, the sewing classes, the soup kitchens, the health programmes, the Memorial House on East Sixteenth Street built in 1886. New York called it Morgan's Church while he sat in it. He was married here in 1865 to Fanny, who survives him. The service is Episcopal and plain. Outside, the streets have been held for the procession.
suggested_refs: The St. George Memorial House, 207 East 16th Street, built 1886

stops.name: Wall Street, the two hours
stops.date_confidence: attested to April 1913; the day is not given in the research pool and is defaulted to 01, matching the funeral stop
stops.campa: Flags come down to half-staff along the street and the New York Stock Exchange closes for two hours while the procession passes, an honour the exchange has otherwise reserved for the deaths of presidents of the United States and granted here to a private banker who held no office at all. The house at Wall and Broad has been J. P. Morgan and Company since Drexel died in 1895. It is a partnership of men now, and his son takes it. The exchange reopens at noon and the tape runs on.
suggested_refs: The New York Stock Exchange minutes for the day of Morgan's funeral

stops.name: Cedar Hill, Hartford: the plot four miles from Asylum Street
stops.date_confidence: burial at Cedar Hill is attested to 1913 and the geography lens gives April; the day is unknown and defaulted to 01. Coordinate corrected to Wikipedia's value for the cemetery at 453 Fairfield Avenue; the research pool's geography lens placed it about 4 km east in Hartford's South End, while its afterlife lens already carried the correct pair. The Keller monument's design and the Ark of the Covenant tradition come from the cemetery record and are undated there
stops.campa: He is buried in the family plot at Cedar Hill, a few miles south of the house on Asylum Street where he was born, under a monument of red granite that the architect George Keller designed, by report, to recall the Ark of the Covenant. The cemetery record carries the design and the tradition alike without a date. His father has lain here since 1890. The library on Madison Avenue passes to his son, who opens it to the public in 1924 as a memorial to him and leaves Belle da Costa Greene in charge of it.
suggested_refs: The Morgan monument at Cedar Hill Cemetery, George W. Keller, architect
